messages.author: fbff4100433066b4
messages.subject: Naming Index
parts:
I have been looking for ways to name my indices for parameters; by defalut these are integers. For example, if the parameter beta, say, whose I am trying to estimate is a matrix. The summary of fitted model gives me the following:

                    mean
beta[1,1]   1.382788e-01
beta[1,2]   1.689701e-01
beta[1,3]   6.088898e-02
beta[1,4]   1.003492e-01
beta[2,1]   5.635914e-02
beta[2,2]   1.958766e-01
beta[2,3]   5.372803e-02
beta[2,4]   9.211320e-02
beta[3,1]   1.009675e-01
beta[3,2]   2.057749e-01
beta[3,3]   4.243510e-02
beta[3,4]   1.214053e-01
beta[4,1]   8.676242e-02
beta[4,2]   2.086204e-01
beta[4,3]   5.787311e-02
beta[4,4]   1.161954e-01
beta[5,1]   9.160001e-02
beta[5,2]   1.208747e-01
beta[5,3]   5.406022e-02
beta[5,4]   7.370221e-02
beta[6,1]   7.625002e-02
beta[6,2]   9.775908e-02
beta[6,3]   7.226615e-02
beta[6,4]   5.062221e-02

Now beta is actually a 4 x 6 matrix with names for both rows and columns ('A', 'B', 'C', 'D') x ('XY', 'YZ', 'ZX', 'UV', 'VW', 'WU'). How can I get a nice matrix or data.frame of mean for beta from model fit object. As of now, I am parsing the strings "beta[i, j]" on common and brackets to build a melt data.frame. Any comments and suggestions are welcome. 

Thank you for your time.

regards,
vishy

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Naming Index
parts:
On Friday, October 7, 2016 at 10:03:30 AM UTC-4, Vishv Jeet wrote:
Now beta is actually a 4 x 6 matrix with names for both rows and columns ('A', 'B', 'C', 'D') x ('XY', 'YZ', 'ZX', 'UV', 'VW', 'WU'). How can I get a nice matrix or data.frame of mean for beta from model fit object. As of now, I am parsing the strings "beta[i, j]" on common and brackets to build a melt data.frame. Any comments and suggestions are welcome.

beta <- extract(stanfit, pars = "beta")[[1]]

Ben

messages.author: fbff4100433066b4
messages.subject: Re: Naming Index
parts:
Thanks Ben, 

This gives me beta as an array of size (4000, 6, 4) on which I can run the following to get mean and sd as:

R> mu <- apply(beta, c(2, 3), mean)
R> std <- apply(beta, c(2, 3), sd)

to get 6x4 matrices mu and std which can be given row and column names.

This is helpful.

Thanks.
